item.title: Passion, Focus, and the Power of Slow Growth
item.description: Focus on the Core and Eliminate Distractions As an entrepreneur, your scarcest resources are time and attention. In an era of information overload, where trends and technologies evolve rapidly, chasing every “opportunity” will only dilute your focus and lead you astray. Real success often comes from doubling down on the core, saying no to everything else. When Steve Jobs returned to Apple, he made sweeping cuts to the product line and redirected the company’s resources toward a few core projects.

item.title: Mastering Simplification: The Art of Focus, Leverage, and Resilience
item.description: What is Simplification? Simplification is a core practice in the era of Moore’s Law. By focusing on simplification, it enhances efficiency, prioritizes critical issues, and uncovers higher-value solutions in complex and dynamic environments. Classic Simplification Focus on the Primary Contradiction Core Idea: Focus on solving “the most important task” and avoid distractions. Common Problems with Multiple Objectives: Chasing easy tasks while ignoring truly valuable creations. Fragmented efforts turn simple problems into complex ones.

item.title: Reading Notes on *Deng Xiaoping and the Transformation of China*
item.description: Crossing the River by Feeling the Stones In 1978, there was no clear blueprint for achieving national strength and wealth. However, Deng Xiaoping had two critical realizations for moving forward: Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan were experiencing rapid development. Their paths could not be entirely copied. Key approaches: Gradually establishing various systems instead of immediately opening markets. Encouraging cadres to broaden their horizons and learn from successful experiences worldwide.
